hanb boards are hexagonal with 61 cells, each containing one of 64 possible characters.
The hanb alphabet uses a-z, A-Z, 0-9, '-' and '.' -- 64 characters total.
Each hanb board represents a finite space at a scale between 0 and 63.
'a' represents quantum foam and '.' represents a universe -- the full range of scales.
Boards can be written as 61-character compressed strings.
The hanb system has 64 levels, yielding 61^64 cells or 64^64 combinations with return values.
Board sizes increase by a factor of 10 with each character step.
'A' = 1 Angstrom (10^-10 m), roughly the size of an atom.
'K' = 1 meter, roughly the size of a person.
'.' = 1 Rm = 10^27 m, roughly the size of the observable universe.
A planet at size 'R' inside a galaxy of size '6' is addressed as a path string like '6543210ZYXWVUTSKu3923sderfdewW'.
The return value of a hanb board is a 3-character string coded as '9-.'.
Hanb boards can be rotated -- the hexagon rotations are 90 degrees different from cell orientations.
Multiple universes can be transmitted as a universe matrix using the '#' character.
Queries on 'a' (quantum foam) particles return a random value.
'u' represents a quark at ~100 attometers (10^-16 m).
'v' represents a proton at 1 femtometer -- classical proton radius is ~0.84 fm.
'S' = planet-moon system at 100 Mm, about 1 light-second.
'T' = 1 Gm, roughly the diameter of the Sun.
'X' = complete star system at 10 Tm, about 1 light-day.
A single location string for any object is inversely proportional to its size.
Hanb was designed by handyc as a toy universe modeling language.
Hanb can be used with or without a computer -- if you know the alphabet, you can use hanb.
The smallest 'a' objects (quantum foam particles) have the longest location strings.
Objects at each level can combine to form the next higher-level particle.
Hanb can be used for computer games, social simulations, terrain visualizations, and more.
The path from quantum foam to universe: a -> b -> c -> ... -> Z -> 0 -> 1 -> ... -> 9 -> - -> .
'9' represents a large supercluster at about 1 billion light years across.
'-' represents a cosmic filament at about 10 billion light years.
A universe in position N of a universe matrix is addressed simply as the string 'N'.
Hanb boards support two text rotations: edge-up and point-up hexagonal display.
Each cell on a hanb board can be interpreted as a smaller board at the next level of detail.
The hanb coordinate system uses the alphabet to reference each of the 61 physical cells plus 3 return values.
